draft.title: Multiple narrators
card: Some texts are told by several narrators in turn. A novel might hand each chapter to a different character, who tells that part in their own voice.
Each narrator gives a partial view. They only know what they have seen, heard or been told, and they tell it through their own feelings and beliefs.
The reader builds a fuller picture by comparing the narrators. Where two accounts agree, the reader can be more confident. Where they differ, the reader asks why.
For example, one narrator calls an argument a harmless joke, while another remembers being hurt. Neither tells the whole story, but together they show more than either could alone.
draft.remember: Each narrator sees only part of the story, so the reader compares them to see more.

a.q: Why might an author tell a story through several narrators in turn?
opts: Each gives a partial view, so readers can compare them
One narrator always knows more than all the others
It lets the author speak directly to the reader
It makes sure every narrator is honest and reliable
a.why: Each narrator sees only part of events, so the reader gains a fuller picture by comparing them. It is wrong to think one narrator always knows more: the card says each view is partial.
a.clue: Think about what the reader does with the different accounts.

b.q: In a novel, Priya says the school camp was a great success. In the next chapter, her friend Tom describes feeling left out and lonely at the same camp. What does the reader gain from reading both chapters?
opts: A fuller picture, as each shows a different part
The truth, because Tom's account cancels out Priya's
Proof that Priya is lying about the camp
A single view, because both narrators agree on events
b.why: Priya and Tom each give a partial view, and comparing them shows that the camp felt different to each of them. It is tempting to say Priya is lying, but a different experience does not mean she is dishonest.
b.clue: A difference between accounts does not always mean someone is lying.

a.best: Each gives a partial view, so readers can compare them

b.best: A fuller picture, as each shows a different part
